display_name: Blue-Chip RSI Reversion — Wide Sector Book
thesis: Mechanism: a 14-day RSI reading below 30 in a mature, high-float, heavily-owned single stock that is still trading above its 150-day SMA is short-horizon, largely non-fundamental selling pressure inside an intact intermediate trend -- single-name news overreaction (a guidance miss, a downgrade, a lawsuit headline), index-fund and closet-indexer rebalancing flow that is price-insensitive by construction, and short-term momentum/CTA selling that fades once the news cycle clears. These are mature large-caps with active buyback programs and broad analyst coverage, which put a latent, valuation-aware bid under the stock once the panic-driven flow is done -- buyback desks, value-tilted funds and short-term dip buyers are the counterparty I am trading against, buying from forced or reflexive sellers who are not pricing the business, and selling to them (via the RSI>55 exit) once sentiment normalizes but before the move can be mistaken for a fresh trend leg. The 150-day trend filter is the same 'nothing structural has changed yet' proxy used elsewhere in this round, just faster than a 200-day filter because single stocks re-rate faster than diversified ETFs. Pre-registered failure regime: a fast, deep, systemic decline where 150-day SMAs across the whole book have not yet turned down before the crash accelerates (COVID's Feb-Mar 2020 leg is the clearest historical case in my own sample; GFC's Sep-Oct 2008 leg is the plausible second case, though I have only one qualifying signal in that exact window). In that regime the entry keeps firing on 'dips' that are actually the first third of a systemic decline correlated across every name in the book at once -- the diversification this book is built on works against single-stock idiosyncratic risk but does nothing against a market-wide air pocket -- so the RSI>55 exit does not arrive inside the 15-day hold, several positions hit the 7% stop simultaneously, and losses cluster in the same handful of sessions rather than being spread out.
